title: August and the Mixtape
premise: When Yara Quintana's family moves to the fading mill town of Halloway, she plans to survive senior year unnoticed at Ashford High, a school built atop the ruins of a shuttered textile factory. But her late grandmother's recipe box holds a cassette mixtape and a recipe card that reads like instructions for breaking into the school's sealed sub-basement. Following them, Yara uncovers evidence that the school board knowingly built over toxic waste that has been sickening students for decades—including her grandmother, who died gathering proof. As the board closes in to destroy the records before the anniversary dedication ceremony, Yara must choose between protecting her new friends' futures and telling a truth that could burn the town down. In the end, she broadcasts the tape during the ceremony, forcing an investigation, honoring her grandmother's inheritance of stubborn love.
about_author: Oscar Ishikawa is a former high school custodian who spent years listening to the stories buildings keep in their walls. He writes young adult fiction about ordinary kids who refuse to look away, and lives near a river that remembers more than it says.

chapters.title: Fine, Obviously
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Moving into Grandma Rosa's old house, Yara catalogs everything wrong with Halloway while insisting to her mother she's fine with the move, the school, all of it. Emotional beat: brittle denial masking grief and dread about being the new kid again.

chapters.title: The Recipe Box
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Unpacking the kitchen, she finds Grandma Rosa's recipe box and a card labeled 'For the ones who come after'—directions involving the school's east stairwell, not food. Emotional beat: eerie curiosity cracking open her guarded grief.

chapters.title: Ashford High Has No Basement
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. First day at Ashford High; friendly outcast Dev Patel gives her the unofficial tour and jokes that the school 'doesn't have a basement,' which everyone repeats too quickly. Emotional beat: alienation laced with the first spark of belonging.

chapters.title: Cardamom and Concrete Dust
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Testing one of Rosa's actual recipes, Yara notices the spice measurements form numbers—a date: 1987—and a locker combination. Emotional beat: wonder turning to unease as coincidence stops being plausible.

chapters.title: Locker 114
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The combination opens a forgotten locker near the east stairwell containing a student ID for Marisol Quintana—Rosa's sister, erased from family stories. Emotional beat: betrayal; her grandmother lied by omission.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Wasn't in the Yearbook
chapters.summary: Alternating Yara/Dev POV. Dev helps Yara dig through archives; Marisol's photo has been cut from every yearbook after 1986. Emotional beat: alliance forming, two lonely kids finding purpose together.

chapters.title: Sick Season
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Classmate Priya collapses with respiratory failure—the third case this semester. Teachers exchange looks; Principal Voss announces a 'wellness initiative.' Emotional beat: dread hardening into suspicion.

chapters.title: What the Mill Left Behind
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev, whose father worked demolition on the old Halbrook Textile Mill, recalls crews hauling drums from the site weeks before the school was poured. Emotional beat: guilt—he'd been told never to ask questions.

chapters.title: Side A
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Beneath the recipe cards she finds a cassette labeled 'M + R, forever.' A pawnshop tape deck plays Rosa's teenage voice describing 'what they buried under the gym floor.' Emotional beat: her grandmother alive again, urgent and furious.

chapters.title: The Dedication Committee
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara volunteers for the school's 40th anniversary committee to access restricted areas, landing directly under board chair Eleanor Voss's polished smile. Emotional beat: terror disguised as confidence; first real contact with the antagonist.

chapters.title: Instructions Not for Food
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Decoding more recipe cards, Yara maps a route through maintenance corridors to a sealed sub-basement door stamped HALBROOK MILL — DO NOT ENTER. Emotional beat: threshold fear; no going back once she knows the way.

chapters.title: Below the Gym Floor
chapters.summary: Yara and Dev POV, alternating. They breach the sub-basement: corroded drums, a makeshift shrine Marisol left, and her notebook documenting contamination and the board's cover-up. Emotional beat: awe curdling into horror.

chapters.title: Marisol
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The notebook reveals Marisol got sick, was discredited as 'unstable,' and died at nineteen while Rosa kept collecting evidence too afraid to publish. Emotional beat: grief reframed—Rosa wasn't a liar but a survivor drowning in guilt.

chapters.title: Someone Followed Us
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Footprints and a relocked padlock prove someone knows they were below. Voss offers Dev's father a promotion contingent on 'keeping his kid focused.' Emotional beat: paranoia; loyalty tested by economic threat.

chapters.title: Loyalty Is a Loaded Word
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev's father begs him to drop it; Dev must decide whether protecting his family means abandoning the truth. Emotional beat: heartbreak—the cost of doing right is never abstract.

chapters.title: The Quiet Offer
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Voss privately offers Yara a college recommendation and her mother a stable job if she returns what she 'borrowed.' Emotional beat: temptation; duty to family versus duty to the dead.

chapters.title: Everything Is Not Fine
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara confesses everything to her mother, expecting fury; instead Mom reveals Rosa's dying words: 'Finish it.' Emotional beat: catharsis; the family secret becomes a shared inheritance.

chapters.title: Copy Everything
chapters.summary: Group POV (Yara, Dev, Priya's brother Marcus). The friends digitize the notebook and duplicate the tape, distributing copies as insurance before the anniversary ceremony. Emotional beat: resolve; fear transmuted into strategy.

chapters.title: Locked Out
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The sub-basement is concreted overnight and the recipe box stolen from her house; Voss announces the archive room will be sealed permanently after the ceremony. Emotional beat: despair at its lowest point—the truth nearly buried for good.

chapters.title: Side B
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Discovering the tape's second side—Marisol's own voice, naming every board member complicit—Yara realizes the ceremony's sound system is her last chance. Emotional beat: fierce clarity; the plan crystallizes.

chapters.title: Play It Loud
chapters.summary: Multi-POV climax. During the dedication, Yara swaps the ceremonial audio feed; Marisol's voice fills the auditorium as Dev live-streams and Marcus hands documents to a reporter. Voss's collapse, the crowd's roar, sirens outside. Emotional beat: triumphant chaos; the buried finally heard.

chapters.title: For the Ones Who Come After
chapters.summary: Yara's POV epilogue. Months later: state investigation launched, remediation ordered, a memorial plaque for Marisol unveiled. Yara adds her own card to the recipe box and passes the tradition forward. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace; inheritance fulfilled, not ended.
